messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: openCR 1.3.0
parts: openCR 1.3.0 is now on CRAN. This release (the first on CRAN since 1.2.0 in May) fixes various bugs and adds minor new features (control over sample size for AIC, a summary method for openCR objects, detector-specific learned responses bk etc.).  Names of existing learned responses have been moved around (e.g., bsession now refers to a within-session effect; see openCR-vignette.pdf for details). openCR-examples.pdf has been revised. For a list of changes see here.

messages.author: e14baef37a11434f
messages.subject: Re: openCR 1.3.0
parts:
Hello,

I am using openCR 1.3.2, and am experiencing an error I had faced in earlier versions, openCR 1.1 I believe. The issue is that trap covariates seem to not work and can’t be found. I had a version that did work (openCR 1.2.1), but as I say it doesn’t seem to now. Anyone else experiencing this behaviour?

Cheers,
Clayton

> head(covariates(traps(grizzCH$Southern_Rockies_2006)))

598306_5579452        BS
598724_5563896        BS
601172_5542114        BS
601647_5508515        BS
602758_5517775        BS
> osecr.mult13trap.lambda <- openCR.fit(capthist = grizzCH, mask= GBmask.o, type = 'JSSAsecrlCL',

parts:
That doesn't tell us where Trap_Type came from...

But I have added the necessary line (one line!) to the code and repackaged it as pre-release 1.3.3 that you can get from www.otago.ac.nz/density/zip/openCR_1.3.3.tar.gz (no Windows binary yet, but it seems you can do without). Hope this solves your problem - good to get some long jobs running over Christmas?
Murray

library(openCR)  # >= 1.3.3

# fake a trap covariate
covariates(traps(captdata)) <- data.frame(Trap_type = sample.int(2,100, replace = TRUE))
# test
msk <- make.mask(traps(captdata))
fit <- openCR.fit(captdata, type='secrCL', model = lambda0 ~ Trap_type, mask = msk)
coef(fit)
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(Trap_type=1:2))

# > coef(fit)
#                          beta    SE.beta        lcl        ucl
